messages.author: 6a288128bce8283d
messages.subject: detection history correlated over time
parts:
Hello all,

I recently talked to someone about the occu model derived from
MacKenzie et al. (2002) and that person raised concerns about temporal
correlation of detection probabilities. Now I would like to ask your
input on this:

If there are 3 visits per site then the probability of a series in
time would be something like:

P(Yi1) * P(Yi2|Yi1) * P(Yi3|Yi2)

as far as I understand it the paper assumed independence over time in
the sense of:

P(Yi1) * P(Yi2) * P(Yi3)

as the repeat measures are used to generate the detection
probabilities.

Are these assumptions correct?
If so: how big of an impact could this be on the model results and are
there any suggestions of dealing with this?

Thank you for your help,
Richard

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] detection history correlated over time
parts:
hi Richard,
 It is relatively easy to build-in temporal dependence in the encounter histories using what people usually call a "behavioral response". You might have:

 logit(p[i,t]) = a0 + a1*y[i,t-1]

so that if y[i,t-1] = 1 then there is some increase or decrease in detection probability. This is called an "ephemeral" behavioral response -- termed that by one of Anne Chao's grad students in a Biometrics article around 2005 or 2006.

 The standard behavioral response is something like:

 logit(p[i,t]) = a0 + a1*(if individual was ever captured previously).

Other models seem plausible as well.

regards
andy
